content.value_statement: GDPR projects need clear controls for consent, rights requests, retention, and breach response. This skill gives practical patterns and checklists for privacy-aware system design.
actual_capabilities: Explains GDPR personal data categories, lawful bases, and data subject rights.
Provides consent management patterns for recording, checking, and auditing consent.
Outlines DSAR workflows for access, erasure, rectification, and portability requests.
Shows retention, minimization, anonymization, and privacy-by-design implementation patterns.
Includes breach notification logic and a GDPR implementation checklist.
limitations: It does not replace legal advice from a qualified privacy professional.
Code samples are illustrative and need adaptation before production use.
It does not connect to live systems or verify real compliance state.
It focuses on GDPR and does not cover every global privacy law.

use_cases.title: Design consent tracking
use_cases.description: Plan how an application records consent, stores consent history, and respects withdrawal by purpose.

use_cases.title: Prepare a DSAR process
use_cases.description: Define access, erasure, and portability workflows with deadlines, verification steps, and audit records.

use_cases.title: Review privacy readiness
use_cases.description: Use checklists to compare system controls against GDPR expectations for transparency, security, and breach response.

prompt_templates.title: Map GDPR obligations
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a new product feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature description for GDPR obligations. Identify personal data, lawful bases, consent needs, and data subject rights impacts.

prompt_templates.title: Design consent management
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a consent management flow for analytics and marketing. Include consent records, withdrawal handling, audit history, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a DSAR workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational process design for privacy requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DSAR workflow for access, erasure, and portability requests. Include identity verification, deadlines, exceptions, data sources, and audit logging.

prompt_templates.title: Review privacy architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced system design review before launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this architecture for GDPR privacy by design. Assess minimization, retention, encryption, access controls, breach response, and documentation gaps.

output_examples.input: A product team wants to add marketing analytics to an EU user onboarding flow.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify consent requirements, separate necessary and optional purposes, suggest audit records, and flag withdrawal handling requirements.

output_examples.input: A support team needs a process for data access and erasure requests.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline verification, deadline tracking, source-by-source data collection, deletion exceptions, response logging, and portability export needs.

output_examples.input: An engineering team wants to reduce stored personal data in analytics events.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend minimization, pseudonymized identifiers, location generalization, retention limits, and anonymization for old records.

best_practices: Document the lawful basis and retention period for each processing activity.
Separate consent by purpose and make withdrawal as easy as giving consent.
Validate examples with legal, security, and engineering reviewers before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not preselect optional consent choices or bundle unrelated purposes together.
Do not retain personal data without a defined purpose, owner, and deletion rule.
Do not treat sample workflows as proof of legal compliance without local review.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and review structure, but legal counsel should validate compliance decisions.

faq.question: Can it help with consent banners?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives patterns for consent categories, opt-in choices, audit records, and withdrawal handling.

faq.question: Does it handle data subject access requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers access, erasure, rectification, portability, verification, deadlines, and exception handling.

faq.question: Can it audit a live production system?
faq.answer: No. It can guide review questions and checklists, but it does not inspect live infrastructure.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it limited to GDPR?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on GDPR concepts and should be supplemented for other privacy regimes.
